check.population: every class, module and package boundary in the codebase
check.freshness: a verdict stands until the module's contents, exports or imports change
check.refusal: the dependency, visibility or clone rule fails the build on the change that breaks the property
check.observation: cohesion, coupling, duplication and export metrics read from source and the import graph
check.evidence: none: the catalog states this check as a class, so a watched run belongs to each system that adopts it
check.authority: the declared module boundary, which every import and export conforms to

distinctFrom.reason: Single responsibility limits a module's reasons to change, while interface segregation limits what a client depends on.
Single responsibility limits reasons to change, while the open/closed principle governs adding behavior without editing.
Single responsibility limits what one part does, while composability governs how parts combine.
Single responsibility is one reason to change per class or module, while separation of concerns separates the named concerns of a system.

records.name: Single Responsibility Principle (SRP)
records.definition: A design rule that a class or module has one reason to change, because it serves one responsibility.

distinctFrom.reason: Separation of concerns splits code by responsibility, while one concern per file binds each file to one declared role tag.
Separation of concerns decides where concerns live, while the open/closed principle decides how behavior is added.
Separation of concerns keeps concerns apart, while composability lets parts combine.

records.name: Separation of Concerns
records.definition: A design rule that parsing, business logic, persistence and presentation each live in their own part of the code.

records.name: Do Not Repeat Yourself (DRY)
records.definition: A design rule that each piece of logic, constant or schema has one source in the code, and every other use refers to it.

distinctFrom.reason: High cohesion is members sharing one purpose, while over-specialization is the reuse lost by narrowing that purpose too far.

records.name: High Cohesion
records.definition: The degree to which the members of a class or module work on the same data towards the same purpose.

distinctFrom.reason: Low coupling is about the dependencies between modules, while high cohesion is about the purpose inside one.
Low coupling limits how far a change ripples between modules, while portability is running on another platform unchanged.
Low coupling limits how far a change spreads, while replaceability is swapping an implementation without editing its callers.
Low coupling is few forced changes between modules, while stable interfaces are signatures that keep across releases.
Low coupling concerns change between modules, while testability is running code in isolation with supplied dependencies.
Low coupling applies between any modules, while domain purity keeps the domain model free of infrastructure concerns.

records.name: Low Coupling
records.definition: The degree to which a module can change without forcing changes in the modules around it.

distinctFrom.reason: Encapsulation guards an object's state behind its operations, while abstraction expresses what a thing does without how.
Encapsulation protects state and its invariants, while information hiding keeps implementation decisions private behind an interface.
Encapsulation guards state, while single responsibility limits a module to one reason to change.
Encapsulation controls how state changes, while immutability forbids change after creation.
Encapsulation protects existing state, while the open/closed principle governs how new behavior is added.
Encapsulation limits writes to an object's own operations, while state isolation limits writes to one unit of concurrent execution.

records.name: Encapsulation
records.definition: A design rule that an object's state is changed only through its own operations, which keep its invariants.

records.name: Information Hiding
records.definition: A design rule that a module exposes an interface and keeps the implementation decisions behind it private.

distinctFrom.reason: Abstraction expresses a concept by what it does, while dependency inversion fixes that the high-level policy owns that expression.
Abstraction hides how a thing works behind what it does, while DRY keeps one source for each piece of logic.
Abstraction is the general rule, while interface-based design applies it to module dependencies supplied from outside.
Abstraction hides detail, while inversion of control moves object creation and control flow to a framework or composition root.
Abstraction hides detail, while the open/closed principle adds behavior at an extension point without editing existing code.
Abstraction separates what from how, while separation of concerns separates parsing, logic, persistence and presentation.

records.name: Abstraction
records.definition: A design rule that a concept is expressed by what it does for the code that uses it, and the detail of how it does it stays out of that expression.

distinctFrom.reason: Modularity divides a system into cohesive parts, while autonomy gives each owner its own data and decisions.
Modularity divides a system, while composability lets its parts combine.
Modularity is division into modules, while encapsulation protects one object's state.
Modularity divides the system, while the open/closed principle governs adding behavior at an extension point.
Modularity is the rule to divide, while package by feature chooses the axis of division, the feature.
Modularity divides into cohesive modules, while separation of concerns names which concerns must not share a part.
Modularity is the division of a system, while single responsibility limits one class or module to one reason to change.

records.name: Modularity
records.definition: A design rule that a system is divided into cohesive modules with explicit boundaries and few dependencies between them.

distinctFrom.reason: Composability lets parts combine through compatible interfaces, while DRY keeps one source for each piece of logic.

records.name: Composability
records.definition: A design rule that parts share compatible interfaces and carry no hidden side effects, so they can be combined into larger parts.

records.name: Composition Over Inheritance
records.definition: A design rule that behavior is reused by holding and delegating to another object instead of extending its class.

distinctFrom.reason: Reusability serves new callers unchanged, while over-generalization is the clarity lost by making code serve every case.

records.name: Reusability
records.definition: The degree to which a function or module can serve a new caller without change, because it carries no context of its first one.

exemplar.before:
function saveAdminFoo(foo: Foo) { return adminFooDb.insert(foo); }
function savePublicFoo(foo: Foo) { return publicFooDb.insert(foo); }

distinctFrom.reason: Replaceability is swapping an implementation, while high cohesion is members sharing one purpose.
Replaceability is substituting one implementation when the code changes, while interchangeability is selecting among several live implementations at runtime.
Replaceability swaps one component, while portability moves the whole software to another platform.
Replaceability puts a new implementation behind the same callers, while reusability serves a new caller with the same implementation.
Replaceability swaps an implementation in production, while testability supplies dependencies in a test.
Replaceability swaps what sits behind an interface, while stable interfaces keep the interface itself unchanged across releases.
Replaceability makes one kind of change cheap, while maintainability is the ease of every kind of correction and extension.

records.name: Replaceability
records.definition: The degree to which a component can be swapped for another implementation of its interface without editing its callers.

distinctFrom.reason: Interchangeability lets implementations be swapped, while specialized optimization is the tuning for one implementation that it gives up.

records.name: Interchangeability
records.definition: The degree to which several implementations conform to one contract closely enough to be selected at runtime.

exemplar.after:
interface FooStore { find(id: FooId): Promise<Foo | undefined>; }
function loadFoo(store: FooStore, id: FooId) { return store.find(id); }

records.name: Independence
records.definition: A design rule that a module can be tested and deployed without the modules around it being present or released.

distinctFrom.reason: Autonomy is ownership of data and decisions, while explicit contracts are the declared boundaries others use to reach them.
Autonomy leaves decisions with their owner, while governance holds decisions to shared policy.
Autonomy lets each owner choose, while standardization fixes one choice everywhere.
Autonomy is one unit owning its data and decisions, while decentralization is the system-wide placement of control with those units.
Autonomy is ownership, while independence is being tested and deployed without the neighboring modules.

records.name: Autonomy
records.definition: A design rule that a service or team owns its data and decisions, so it alone writes its data and others reach or change it only through its published API or events.
